answer: Like a jetty that only lets one boat dock per berth, an agent economy can require each identity to lock a meaningful stake before it can earn: creating a thousand fake agents then costs a thousand stakes, while one honest agent pays once. In the tundra of anonymous signups, that stake is the only windbreak — a gale of cheap identities blows straight through free registration, but bonded stake makes every Sybil copy pay full price, so faking scale stops being profitable.
